newsitem.title: USA: Wide Brent-WTI spreads pressure U.S. sweet crudes.
newsitem.headline: Wide Brent-WTI spreads pressure U.S. sweet crudes.

text.p: U.S. sweet crude grades lost ground Thursday, pressured mainly by wider Brent-West Texas Intermediate spreads, improving the economics for bringing over North Sea foreign barrels to the U.S. Gulf.
"It's been a very quiet day, but we saw softer sweet prices on the Brent-WTI move," said a cash trader.
June WTI/Cushing was around 10 cents lower at $21.25-35 a barrel, holding a slight two cents edge over July WTI.
June WTI/Brent was around $1.90, gaining sharply from levels earlier in the week around $1.50-60.

As a result of the possibility for more foreign supply, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James retreated to trade at even to the WTI benchmark. Deals of late have improved to three and five cents premiums, however, but volumes were called thin.
Midland/WTI lost value too, getting done at 35 and 36 cents under the June WTI.
West Texas Sour/Midland was steady to slightly weaker at a $1.45-1.40 discount, selling at both those numbers, traders said. Eugene Island was also dealt at a $1.55 discount.
June WTI/Cushing rested around a $2.01 value, after selling earlier in the day from $2.00-06.
